quote.quote: A meeting of the Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee was held on November 2, 2012 to discuss the BLA for raxibacumab.

meeting_date.text: November 2, 2012 (a prior first-cycle AC meeting was held October 27, 2009; the November 2, 2012 meeting was for the resubmission that led to approval)

quote.quote: A meeting of the Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee was held on November 2, 2012 to discuss the BLA for raxibacumab.

recommendation.text: At the November 2, 2012 meeting the committee voted 16 yes / 1 no / 1 abstention that the animal studies provide substantial evidence of likely clinical benefit for treatment, and 18 yes / 0 no / 0 abstention that the safety data support an acceptable risk-benefit profile. The product was approved.

quote.quote: There were 16 committee members who voted yes, 1 voted no, and 1 abstention.

linkages.concern: At the first-cycle advisory committee (October 27, 2009), the panel found the high survival with antibacterial drug alone obscured any added benefit of raxibacumab and recommended that additional data be obtained to evaluate the added benefit (or possible antagonism) of raxibacumab combined with antimicrobials in an animal model.
linkages.change: The Complete Response Letter required, and the applicant then conducted for the resubmission, an additional animal study (the Added Benefit Study, 1141-CG920871) to demonstrate the added benefit of raxibacumab when used with an antibacterial drug.

concern_quote.quote: At the Anti-infective Drug Committee Advisory Committee convened on October 27, 2009 to discuss the data on raxibacumab's efficacy in animal models and its safety in animals and human volunteers, the panel recommended additional information be obtained to evaluate added benefit or possible antagonism of raxibacumab on antimicrobials in animal models.

change_quote.quote: an additional study in a model of inhalational anthrax to demonstrate the added benefit of raxibacumab when used with an antibacterial drug

linkages.concern: Several members of the November 2, 2012 advisory committee opined that raxibacumab could be of benefit for post-exposure prophylaxis, particularly if a drug-resistant strain of B. anthracis were released and antibacterial drugs could not be relied upon.
linkages.change: The reviewer recommended broadening the labeled indication to include prophylaxis of inhalational anthrax when alternative therapies are not available or are not appropriate; the approved label carries this prophylaxis indication.

concern_quote.quote: Several members of the Advisory Committee (see section 9 of this review) opined that raxibacumab may also be of benefit for post-exposure prophylaxis in the event of release of a strain of *B. anthracis* which is resistant to available antibacterial drugs.

change_quote.quote: Thus, it is reasonable to conclude that raxibacumab used as post-exposure prophylaxis when alternative therapies are not available or are not appropriate would be reasonably likely to produce clinical benefit in exposed persons, and I recommend broadening the labeled indication accordingly.

linkages.concern: Committee members at the November 2, 2012 meeting raised concern about whether concurrent use of raxibacumab and anthrax vaccination might impair vaccine efficacy.
linkages.change: A postmarketing commitment (tied to the prophylaxis indication) was recommended to conduct a Phase 4 study evaluating the effect of raxibacumab on the immunogenicity of anthrax vaccine.

concern_quote.quote: Committee members raised concern regarding whether concurrent use of raxibacumab and anthrax vaccination may impact vaccination efficacy.

change_quote.quote: Conduct a Phase 4 study to evaluate the effect of raxibacumab on immunogenicity of anthrax vaccine.

summary: Raxibacumab (BLA 125349) went before the Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee twice. At the first-cycle meeting (October 27, 2009) the panel recommended an additional animal study to demonstrate the added benefit of raxibacumab combined with an antibacterial drug; this became a Complete Response Letter deficiency that the applicant addressed with the Added Benefit Study in its resubmission. At the resubmission meeting (November 2, 2012) the committee voted 16-1-1 that the animal data showed likely clinical benefit and 18-0-0 that the risk-benefit profile was acceptable, and members further opined raxibacumab could be useful for post-exposure prophylaxis while raising a concern about possible interference with anthrax vaccine immunogenicity; the approval broadened the indication to include prophylaxis and added a Phase 4 postmarketing commitment on vaccine immunogenicity.
